1	# RTK — Token-Optimized Commands (Windows Native)
2	
3	## Tool Selection Matrix
4	
5	| Need | Domain | Tool |
6	|---|---|---|
7	| Read source / config file | Context Domain | Read tool |
8	| Read large log / build output | Token Domain | `rtk read <file>` or `rtk log` |
9	| All shell commands | Token Domain | `rtk <cmd>` (auto-applied by hook) |
10	
11	Token-optimized CLI proxy: **60–90% savings** on noisy dev operations. RTK passes unknown commands through unchanged — prefixing is always safe.
12	
13	## Golden Rule
14	
15	Any Bash command whose output spans more than a few lines requires the `rtk` prefix.
16	
17	```bash
18	rtk git add . && rtk git commit -m "msg" && rtk git push
19	```
20	
21	This machine is **Windows native**: there is no hook auto-rewrite. Use the explicit prefix.
22	
23	## MUST Prefix (no judgment needed)
24	
25	These commands ALWAYS require `rtk` prefix in Bash — regardless of expected output length:
26	
27	| Command | Prefix form |
28	|---|---|
29	| `ls`, `ls -la`, `ls -1` | `rtk ls <path>` |
30	| `find` | `rtk find "*.ext" <path>` |
31	| `grep` / `rg` | `rtk grep <pattern> <path>` |
32	| `git status` | `rtk git status` |
33	| `git log` | `rtk git log` |
34	| `git diff` | `rtk git diff` |
35	| `git add` / `commit` / `push` | `rtk git add / commit / push` |
36	| `npm run` / `pnpm` | `rtk npm run <script>` |
37	| `tsc` | `rtk tsc` |
38	| `docker ps` / `docker logs` | `rtk docker ps / logs` |
39	| `curl` (any) | `rtk curl <url>` |
40	
41	**Never use plain `cat` in Bash** — use the Read tool for source files.
42	**Never use plain `ls` in Bash** — always `rtk ls`.
43	
44	## DO

46	- DO prefix `git`, `docker`, `tsc`, test runners, `find`, log files, `gh pr`, package managers.

53	- DON'T prefix one-line commands (`echo`, `pwd`, single-file `cat`) — RTK adds no value there.

2	
3	This machine runs **Claude Code on Windows native** as the sole AI assistant. All rules below are calibrated to that environment — do not generalize across WSL, Linux, or other AI tools.
4	
5	For the full architecture (drive layout, hooks, retention, compaction, AI tool exclusivity), read `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\ARCHITECTURE.md`.

15	## DON'T
16	
17	- DON'T propose WSL workflows, install steps, or `rtk init -g --auto-patch` hook auto-rewrite. RTK on Windows native is **manual prefix only** — that is the supported model here.
18	- DON'T add hooks, scripts, agents, or rules without a documented recurring need. **FOMO guard**: a feature looking interesting is not justification — point to a past incident or measurable benefit, or skip it.
19	- DON'T deviate from default Claude Code behavior unless an incident or measurable cost forced the customization. **Vanilla compliance**: the closer to stock, the easier upgrades and debugging become.
20	- DON'T relocate the `.claude` config root to D: (e.g. `D:\.claude\`, `D:\.claude-data\`). Global Claude infra lives under `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` on whichever drive holds the user profile. Project work on D: is fine and expected — the prohibition targets splitting the `.claude` infra across drives, not D-drive paths in project content.
21	- DON'T commit or read `.credentials*` files. Don't run destructive git operations (force push, hard reset) unless the user explicitly orders it.
22	- DON'T use destructive shortcuts (`rm -rf`, `--no-verify`, `git push --force`) to bypass an obstacle — fix the root cause.

25	
26	Before saying the task is complete:
27	
28	1. **Restate the order** — paste the user's original request as a one-liner.
29	2. **List acceptance criteria** — what observable state would prove completion?
30	3. **Map criteria → evidence** — for each, cite `file:line`, command output, or test result.
31	4. **Detect scope creep** — anything done outside the order? Justify it or revert.
32	5. **Honor constraints** — language, paths, tools the user specified. Verify each.
33	
34	If any criterion lacks evidence: do **not** declare done. Either complete it or explicitly report the gap.

36	Template: `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\templates\order-match-checklist.md`.

38	## Auto Memory
39	
40	The auto-memory system runs on `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\projects\<project>\memory\MEMORY.md` index plus per-topic `.md` files. Index capped at 200 lines / 25 KB; split into topic files when it grows. Four memory types: user profile, feedback, project context, external-system reference.

43	
44	See `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\templates\project-init.md`. Standard layout (per project): `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `.claude/rules/` / `.claude/agents/` / `.claude/settings.json`. There is no global `AGENTS.md` — that file is per-project only.

51	
52	Configured in `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json`. **7 hook events** (SessionStart, SessionEnd, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, PostCompact, Stop) plus a `statusLine` renderer and one `env` setting. See AUTOMATION.md for the architecture diagram and current registration table.

60	- **statusLine**: cwd-leaf | model | effort | session count | compact warning.
61	- **env**: `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1` only (vanilla baseline). `prefix-version.txt` is bumped on rule changes to invalidate stale cache.

1	# Global Claude Code Architecture
2	
3	This document describes the architecture of this machine's global Claude Code setup. Read this before changing rules, hooks, or directory layout. Companion documents:
4	
5	- `CLAUDE.md` — operating rules (DO / DON'T)
6	- `RTK.md` — token-optimized CLI proxy reference
7	- `AUTOMATION.md` — session automation hooks (architecture diagram + auto-generated tables)
8	- `templates/order-match-checklist.md` — task self-verification template
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. Operating Environment
13	
14	| Property | Value |
15	|---|---|
16	| OS | Windows 10 (native, no WSL) |
17	| Shell | Git Bash (primary) / PowerShell 5.1 |
18	| AI assistant | Claude Code (sole assistant — Codex / Cursor removed) |
19	| IDE host | VS Code with Claude Code extension |
20	| Drive layout | C drive (under `%USERPROFILE%`) for the `.claude` config root. Project work lives on D:; only the Claude infra itself is single-drive. |
21	
22	**Rationale (single-drive on C)**: cognitive simplicity, tool universality (every Windows tool assumes `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`), and vanilla compliance with Claude Code's default. C has 88+ GB free; the entire setup is ~165 MB.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## 2. Directory Layout
27	
28	```
29	%USERPROFILE%\.claude\                     [single source of truth, plain dirs only — no junctions]
30	│
31	├── CLAUDE.md                              # operating rules (DO / DON'T)
32	├── RTK.md                                 # CLI proxy reference
33	├── AUTOMATION.md                          # session automation architecture + auto-marked tables
34	├── ARCHITECTURE.md                        # this file
35	│
36	├── settings.json                          # hook registrations + permissions + statusline
37	├── settings.local.json                    # per-host overrides (optional)
38	├── active-projects.json                   # pinned projects (cleanup.ps1 protection list)
39	├── .claude.json                           # Claude Code internal session state (autogenerated, do not edit)
40	├── .credentials.json                      # MCP auth (sensitive — never read / commit)
41	│
42	├── cleanup.ps1                            # SessionEnd cleanup + retention rotations
43	├── statusline.ps1                         # status line renderer (cwd | model | effort | sessions | warnings)
44	│
45	├── hooks/                                 # SessionStart / SessionEnd / Pre+PostCompact / PostToolUse hooks
46	├── templates/                             # project-init.md, order-match-checklist.md
47	├── plugins/                               # plugin metadata
48	├── ide/                                   # IDE settings
49	├── agents/                                # custom agent definitions (if any)
50	├── commands/                              # slash command definitions (if any)
51	│
52	├── projects/                              # per-project session state + memory
53	├── plans/                                 # active + archived plans
54	├── reports/                               # token-usage.md (append-only)
55	├── backups/                               # precompact-* snapshots + memory-YYYYWW.zip weekly
56	├── file-history/                          # UUID-keyed file version diffs
57	├── shell-snapshots/                       # shell context snapshots
58	├── sessions/                              # session state (ephemeral)
59	├── session-env/                           # SessionStart artifacts (memory-lint.txt, compact-warning.txt)
60	├── paste-cache/                           # clipboard cache (ephemeral)
61	├── downloads/                             # downloaded artifacts
62	├── telemetry/                             # telemetry queue
63	├── cache/                                 # generic cache
64	├── .docs-cache/                           # SHA256 hashes of upstream docs + prefix-version.txt
65	├── .drift-queue/                          # PostToolUse enqueue → drift-detect-worker drain

71	└── rollback-pre-consolidation.zip         # one-shot pre-D-removal snapshot
72	```
73	
74	**Anti-pattern**: do not create NTFS junctions to redirect any subdirectory to another volume. The previous D-split design was reverted because it complicated backup tooling, broke drive-letter assumptions in third-party scripts, and provided no measurable benefit at this data scale.
75	
76	---
77	
78	## 3. Path Resolution Convention
79	
80	Every script and document references the config root via:
81	
82	```powershell
83	$ClaudeRoot = if ($env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) {
84	    $env:CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
85	} else {
86	    Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE '.claude'
87	}
88	```
89	
90	`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is **not set** in any registry scope — the env var fallback exists only to honor user overrides if a future need arises. The default code path always resolves to `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`.
91	
92	In documentation: use `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (Windows-native, expands in cmd / PowerShell / Git Bash) or `~/.claude/` for compactness.
93	
94	**Forbidden**: relocating the `.claude` config root to a non-profile drive (`D:\.claude\`, `D:\.claude-data\`). D-drive paths in project content are fine — the rule targets the infra root, not the project.
95	
96	---
97	
98	## 4. Hook Architecture
99	
100	Seven hook events are registered in `settings.json` (plus a `statusLine` renderer). SessionEnd registers two command entries, so total command count is eight. See `AUTOMATION.md` for the full sequence diagram and the auto-generated registration table.
101	
102	| Event | Purpose | Async |
103	|---|---|---|
104	| SessionStart | regenerate AUTO-marks, auto-pin, memory-lint, weekly memory-backup, 24h doc gate, 60d plan archive, **D-remnant detection → oneshot consolidation** | no |
105	| SessionEnd | retention rotations (13 categories), MEMORY.md link integrity, kill stale workers, drift queue drain | yes |
106	| PostToolUse (Edit\|Write\|Bash) | enqueue edited files / dep-install audits to `.drift-queue` | yes |
107	| UserPromptSubmit | inject git status + recent commits when repo is dirty (skip-when-clean keeps prompt cache warm) | no |
108	| PreCompact | hard-link snapshot of MUST-preserve set into `backups/precompact-<ts>-<sid>` | no |
109	| PostCompact | verify `@import` chains + active plan readability; write `compact-warning.txt` on issues | yes |
110	| Stop | append rtk session stats to `reports/token-usage.md` | yes |
111	| statusLine | render status line (includes `compact:warn` indicator if PostCompact flagged a loss) | (poll) |
112	
113	**Design principle**: each hook runs in <100 ms in the synchronous path. Heavier work (`check-updates-worker`) is spawned detached via `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden`. Detached workers survive parent exit; PowerShell jobs do not.
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 5. Retention Policy
118	
119	Configured in `cleanup.ps1`. Pinned projects (via `active-projects.json`) are exempt from `projects/` rotation.
120	
121	| Directory | Retention | Notes |
122	|---|---|---|
123	| `plans/` | 2 days (file mtime) | drafts; archived plans go to `plans/archive/` after 60d |
124	| `shell-snapshots/` | 7 days | session shell context |
125	| `file-history/` | 14 days (dir mtime) | UUID-keyed |
126	| `projects/` | 30 days (dir mtime) | pinned + 14d grace exempt |
127	| `session-env/` | empty subdirs only | per-session SessionStart outputs |
128	| `backups/precompact-*` | 28 days | pre-compaction snapshots |
129	| `backups/memory-*.zip` | 56 days | weekly memory archive |
130	| `.docs-cache/` | 90 days (file mtime) | SHA hashes regenerable |
131	| `.drift-queue/` | 7 days | post-drain leftovers |
132	| `cache/` | 14 days | generic |
133	| `downloads/` | 30 days | |
134	| `paste-cache/` | 7 days | clipboard |
135	| `telemetry/` | 30 days | |
136	
137	Stale background workers >24h old are killed by command-line pattern match against `<ClaudeRoot>\hooks\`.
138	
139	---
140	
141	## 6. Compaction Policy (REWIND CONTEXT)
142	
143	When Claude Code reaches its context budget and triggers compaction:
144	
145	**MUST preserve** (load-bearing): active plan, all rule files (`CLAUDE.md` / `RTK.md` / `AUTOMATION.md` / `ARCHITECTURE.md`), `settings.json`, per-project active `MEMORY.md`, memory topic files modified within last 30 days.
146	
147	**MAY drop** (regenerable): plans older than 60 days, `.docs-cache/*`, `cleanup.log`, completed prior-turn todos, intermediate exploration output.
148	
149	**Hooks**: `precompact-snapshot.ps1` hard-links the preserve set into `backups/precompact-<ts>-<sid>/`. `postcompact-verify.ps1` validates `@import` chains and active-plan readability — writes `session-env/compact-warning.txt` on failure, which `statusline.ps1` surfaces as `compact:warn`.
150	
151	**Anti-pattern**: snapshotting `sessions/` or `file-history/` "just in case" — unbounded growth with no recovery use case (FOMO trap).
152	
153	---
154	
155	## 7. RTK Strategy (Token Optimization)
156	
157	RTK is a Rust-based CLI output filter (60–90% token savings). On this machine:
158	
159	- **Mode**: explicit prefix only (`rtk <command>`). Hook-based auto-rewrite is a WSL-only feature and is not used here.
160	- **Coverage**: noisy multi-line outputs (`git`, `docker`, `tsc`, test runners, `find`, log files, `gh pr`, package managers).
161	- **Skip**: single-line outputs (`echo`, `pwd`).
162	
163	Detailed savings table: see `RTK.md`.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 8. Order Match Verification
168	
169	Every non-trivial task ends with a self-verification step before the AI declares completion. Procedure (full template at `templates/order-match-checklist.md`):
170	
171	1. Restate the user's order verbatim.
172	2. List acceptance criteria (observable state).
173	3. Map each criterion to evidence (`file:line`, command output, test result).
174	4. Detect scope creep — anything done outside the order? Justify or revert.
175	5. Honor constraints — language (Korean chat / English AI artifacts), paths (no `D:\.claude`), tools, banned actions.
176	
177	If any criterion lacks evidence: do **not** declare done. Either complete the gap or report it explicitly.
178	
179	This rule is the system's primary safeguard against the "AI says done but didn't actually finish" failure mode.
180	
181	---
182	
183	## 9. Vanilla Compliance + FOMO Guard
184	
185	Two principles that govern every change to this setup:
186	
187	### Vanilla compliance
188	
189	The closer to stock Claude Code behavior, the easier upgrades and debugging become. Do **not** customize unless an incident or measurable cost forced it. Document the trigger when adding any non-default rule.
190	
191	Current non-vanilla customizations and their justifications:
192	
193	| Customization | Trigger |
194	|---|---|
195	| `permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"` | productivity in trusted host environment |
196	| 7 hook events (8 command entries — SessionEnd registers 2) in `settings.json` | upstream doc drift, plan rotation, prompt cache invalidation |
197	| `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` env | 1h prompt cache TTL for token efficiency |
198	| `effortLevel = "high"` | model output quality preference |
199	| 13-category retention in `cleanup.ps1` | unbounded growth in volatile dirs |
200	
201	### FOMO guard
202	
203	A feature looking interesting is not justification. Before adding a hook / script / rule / skill / plugin, point to:
204	
205	- a past incident the change prevents, OR
206	- a measurable benefit (token savings, time savings, error reduction)
207	
208	If neither exists: skip it.
209	
210	---
211	
212	## 10. AI Tool Exclusivity
213	
214	Claude Code is the sole AI assistant on this machine.
215	
216	- **Removed**: Codex CLI (`%USERPROFILE%\.codex`), Cursor (`%APPDATA%\Cursor`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cursor-updater`).
217	- **Pending uninstall** (out of architecture scope, user-driven): VS Code extensions `openai.chatgpt-*`, `github.copilot-chat-*`, Cursor app binaries.
218	
219	Rationale: split AI surfaces produce conflicting context, duplicate token costs, and inconsistent rule application. One assistant = one rule set = predictable behavior.
220	
221	---
222	
223	## 11. Language Convention
224	
225	| Audience | Language |
226	|---|---|
227	| User-facing chat replies | Korean |
228	| AI-consumed artifacts (docs, hooks, plans, memory, comments, log lines) | **English** |
229	| Code identifiers, paths, commands, error messages | English (verbatim, regardless of context) |
230	| Quoted user phrases (e.g. "완료" / "done") | preserved as-is in either language |
231	
232	Rationale: AI consumption efficiency. English keeps tokens predictable across models and avoids encoding ambiguity (PowerShell 5.1 ANSI codepage corrupts em-dash and similar non-ASCII glyphs).
